clean_body: Those in the highest seats of power are treating working people as disposable. Our organizing is as urgent as ever. | | | Peter, Federal agents across the country were reportedly told last week that the FBI will no longer investigate violent confrontations involving immigration agents.1 If this change takes effect, investigations would instead fall to an arm of the very same agency whose agents are involved — an agency investigating itself — with no jurisdiction to even examine civil rights violations.1 Without meaningful oversight, the last guardrails of independent accountability are being stripped away. Those in the highest seats of power are treating our lives as disposable — looking out for their own interests and those of their billionaire donors. Meanwhile, our taxpayer dollars fund raises for the very agents harming our neighbors, instead of addressing skyrocketing gas, grocery, and housing costs — solutions that working families need to thrive. But immigrant or not, when federal agents act without independent oversight, no working person in this country is safe. Hi, Peter! Before the weekend gets away from me, I wanted to take a moment to say thank you for all your support – especially during our final FEC deadline push earlier this week.
We are in the middle of one of the most consequential fights of our lifetimes, and knowing you're in this with me makes all the difference.
Over the last year and a half in Washington, I’ve worked to make a real, tangible difference in my constituents' lives. I delivered $11 million in infrastructure funding for this district. I became the first freshman Democrat to pass a bill through the Republican-controlled House floor last year. And I’ve been fighting back against this administration’s cruel ICE tactics and demanding real oversight on ICE detention centers.
I’m so proud of what we’ve accomplished – and I’m just getting started.
I’m running a grassroots campaign, which means I don’t take a dime from corporate PACs or federal lobbyists. Our support comes from everyday people in Minnesota who believe in this work, and who want to play a part in building a better future for our families and communities.
And right now, that support matters more than ever as more pro-MAGA money flows into our state ahead of the primary.
If you weren’t able to pitch in before this past week’s FEC deadline, or you’d like to contribute again before our big end-of-the-month push, you can do so here:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26]
Thanks for everything – more soon.
Kelly

clean_body: [] Hi, Peter! Before the weekend gets away from me, I wanted to take a moment to say thank you for all your support – especially during our final FEC deadline push earlier this week. We are in the middle of one of the most consequential fights of our lifetimes, and knowing you're in this with me makes all the difference. Over the last year and a half in Washington, I’ve worked to make a real, tangible difference in my constituents' lives. I delivered $11 million in infrastructure funding for this district. I became the first freshman Democrat to pass a bill through the Republican-controlled House floor last year. Today we began our Weekend of Action, and I wanted to share my Day One priorities in Congress to ground ourselves in why we’re doing this:

1. End Congressional stock trading. People sent us to serve, not to trade stocks for personal profit. I will push to ban members from trading individual stocks so votes aren’t a payday.

This is the short, practical to-do list I’ll carry with me. It’s what our families need. It’s what our district deserves. If you support this agenda, consider chipping in to my campaign before our Weekend of Action ends tomorrow.

subject: 1,200 killers could walk free. All Shapiro cares about is LeBron James.

body:
The deadline was yesterday, and Shapiro did nothing.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/pPnkMdEGsOa?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
| | | | | | Peter,
Right now, across Pennsylvania, there are families who lost someone to murder.
A mother. A father. A child.
Someone they loved was taken from them in the worst way imaginable.
They went through the trial. They heard the verdict. They watched the sentence come down.
And for years, they carried the weight of that loss knowing that at least one thing was settled: the person responsible would never walk free.
**Yesterday, that certainty was taken away from them.**
The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled in Commonwealth v. Lee that automatic life-without-parole sentences in second-degree murder cases violate the state’s constitution. The court gave the General Assembly 120 days to pass a constitutional remedy.
The state Senate acted. Senators Lisa Baker and Wayne Langerholc authored SB1400, a bipartisan bill endorsed by the Pennsylvania District Attorneys Association and Attorney General Dave Sunday. It passed the Senate. It creates a constitutional sentencing framework that preserves accountability for serious crimes while recognizing varying degrees of participation in felony murder case.
It was a real solution. And it was ready to go.
But Josh Shapiro and House Democrats chose political games over public safety. Josh Shapiro has had every opportunity to lead, yet he has chosen to do nothing in response to the Supreme Court’s ruling.
Rather than demanding action before the deadline, he seemed to have priorities elsewhere.
**Instead of working with the Legislature to get something done, Josh Shapiro was**[**playing Jeopardy**](https://us.list-manage.com/12zrA1R2wIx?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)**and**[**posting about LeBron James on social media.**](https://us.list-manage.com/L8EDBThUKst?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)

On a day that nearly 1,200 murder victims’ families lost the certainty that their love one’s killer would remain behind bars, Josh Shapiro was more worried about promoting his own image.
Because of Josh Shapiro’s failure to lead, nearly 1,200 convicted murderers across Pennsylvania can now begin to challenge their sentences. That means the families of victims — families who have already been through the unimaginable — will be forced back into courtrooms to relive the worst moments of their lives and confront the specter of facing their loved one’s murderer again.
**Shapiro can fix this right now by calling a special session of the General Assembly to demand that the House act on this bipartisan legislation.**
But he isn’t.
That’s because all Josh Shapiro cares about are headlines, celebrity, and promoting himself at any expense.
But we already knew this.
**Josh Shapiro spends millions of your tax dollars promoting his own image every year.**
This is nothing new for Josh Shapiro.
I stand with the victims. I stand with their families. I stand with law enforcement. I stand with our local district attorneys.
**I am calling on Josh Shapiro to stop talking, stop playing celebrity, and do your job.**
Call a special session. Pass SB 1400. Protect the families who have already suffered enough.
**Stop talking, Governor. Do your job.**

Peter, Freedom is being able to go to school, worship, gather, shop, work,_and live_ without fearing a spree shooter will end your life. **But the captured Supreme Court privileges mass shooters over our rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.** The precedents that the Court has set are already wreaking havoc on state legislatures’ attempts to protect their communities from violence. A federal appeals court just threw out New Jersey’s limits on assault weapons and magazines holding more than 10 rounds. For the first time, a federal appeals court struck down a state assault weapons ban on Second Amendment grounds. The NRA is already celebrating. And this could get worse fast. **The Supreme Court has already agreed to hear challenges to assault weapons bans** in Connecticut and the Chicago area next term. If the MAGA justices strike those laws down, mass gatherings across the entire country could be at risk. This is how the captured Court reshapes the country. First, the Supreme Court legislates from the bench to affirm extremist ideology. Then lower courts use that rule to strike down common sense protections that keep people safe. Then the Supreme Court extends that precedent nationwide. **The result is a country where families are less safe, communities have fewer tools to protect themselves, and the gun lobby gets more power than the people who have to live with the consequences. ** The NRA, gun manufacturers, and dark money interests spent decades building power across our courts and institutions. Now we are seeing what that looks like in real life: **fewer protections, more fear, and a government that cannot answer to working people because the Court keeps standing in the way.** The American people are not powerless. But we need to build demand so big that Congress cannot keep treating this captured Court like business as usual. clean_body: New Jersey’s assault weapons limits were just struck down. SCOTUS could take the same logic nationwide. | | Peter, Freedom is being able to go to school, worship, gather, shop, work,and live without fearing a spree shooter will end your life. But the captured Supreme Court privileges mass shooters over our rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. The precedents that the Court has set are already wreaking havoc on state legislatures’ attempts to protect their communities from violence. A federal appeals court just threw out New Jersey’s limits on assault weapons and magazines holding more than 10 rounds. For the first time, a federal appeals court struck down a state assault weapons ban on Second Amendment grounds. The NRA is already celebrating. And this could get worse fast. The Supreme Court has already agreed to hear challenges to assault weapons bans in Connecticut and the Chicago area next term. If the MAGA justices strike those laws down, mass gatherings across the entire country could be at risk. This is how the captured Court reshapes the country. First, the Supreme Court legislates from the bench to affirm extremist ideology. Then lower courts use that rule to strike down common sense protections that keep people safe. Then the Supreme Court extends that precedent nationwide. The result is a country where families are less safe, communities have fewer tools to protect themselves, and the gun lobby gets more power than the people who have to live with the consequences. The NRA, gun manufacturers, and dark money interests spent decades building power across our courts and institutions. Now we are seeing what that looks like in real life: fewer protections, more fear, and a government that cannot answer to working people because the Court keeps standing in the way. The American people are not powerless. But we need to build demand so big that Congress cannot keep treating this captured Court like business as usual. That is why United for Democracy is fighting to reform the Court, repair our democracy, and build a system that answers to working people, not the gun lobby and dark money donors. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

That is why they are coming after me. We are winning, and they know it. **So they file paperwork. And I keep reporting.** [**Please give your most generous gift today**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.), whatever you can, to defend me from these attacks and keep our cameras rolling. Meet one of
Trump’s most dangerous judicial nominees yet: Gregory Cook.

Trump nominated him for a lifetime seat on the federal bench. The scary
part? Cook's record proves he'll say or do whatever it takes to please the
wannabe authoritarian who nominated him.

Cook has called the Republican Party "the last great hope for America,"
written that "ANY REPUBLICAN IS BETTER THAN ANY DEMOCRAT," and argued to
fellow Christian lawyers that their "relationship with Christ predates"
their "bar card."^1

Peter,

In 2023, the nastiest anti-LGBTQ bill I've ever seen landed on my desk. Republicans in the Kentucky legislature even said out loud: this is what's going to beat Andy Beshear.

**I vetoed it anyway. There are some things worth losing over.**

That night, I went on camera because voters deserved to know why, whether they agreed with me or not. I said my faith teaches me every child is a child of God, and I wasn't going to let anyone pick on these kids. If the General Assembly was going to show them hate and rejection, I was going to show them love and acceptance.

The next day, I went to open a new factory and a guy made a beeline toward me and, instead of arguing with me about my decision, he shook my hand. He said, "Governor, I'm not sure I agree with what you did yesterday, but I know you're doing what you think is right." Then he patted me on the back and walked away.

[_**That’s how I won three times in a state Trump carried by more than 30 points – by explaining my “why.” It’s also how we’re going to elect good candidates in tough races everywhere this fall. Will you contribute today to help In This Together PAC stand with leaders who do what’s right, even when it’s hard?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135983007/635964254/753972181?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_FR_Veto_260725_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjlhZThlMTItNDY4OC1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=Kt6e8GhjAxXdqTfS8zkcKYDb9ompxrVcTm2qlbwlzl8=)

I've vetoed every single piece of anti-LGBTQ legislation that's ever reached my desk as governor, including the one folks said would end my career.

Here's what I've learned: when you explain your “why,” which for me is my faith and my family, it gives people grace and space to disagree with you on tough issues and still trust you’re standing on your convictions, and working hard to improve life for all families.

That's how Democrats can win anywhere, and we should be fighting everywhere — not by moving people to the left or to the right, but by moving us all forward.

name: Team Gina
subject: 254 counties who have been failed
body:
One penny for every county in Texas. One movement ready for change.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Texas is a big state.
With **254 counties,** from the Panhandle to the Rio Grande Valley, East Texas to the Hill Country, every community has its own story, its own challenges, and its own vision for the future.
But too many Texans have been left behind by Greg Abbott’s leadership.
**[We’ve got more to say, but first, can you pitch in $2.54 — a penny for each of the 254 counties Abbott has failed?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260725_2_eom254.S-COYk&refcode=em20260725-1663&amount=2.54&t=1&akid=1663%2E299639%2EqczgGC)**

Gina has traveled thousands of miles across Texas, sitting down with voters, listening to their concerns, and hearing what they need from their next governor.
She’s met teachers worried about the future of public education. Families struggling with rising costs. Small business owners trying to keep their doors open. Rural communities fight to have a say in decisions that impact their land, resources, and way of life.
And everywhere she goes, Gina hears the same message: **Texans are ready for leadership that actually shows up.**
Greg Abbott has spent years prioritizing billionaire donors, corporate interests, and political insiders. But this campaign is about something different.
We’re building a Texas where every community has a voice and every family has a chance to thrive.
That’s why we’re building this campaign the grassroots way — one conversation, one supporter, and one county at a time.
**[So, will you pitch in $2.54 for the 254 counties across Texas that are sick of politics as usual and finally elect a leader who’s going to get the job done?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260725_2_eom254.S-COYk&refcode=em20260725-1663&amount=2.54&t=3&akid=1663%2E299639%2EqczgGC)**

Team Gina

subject: I can’t believe Fox News just did this
body:
[ ](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260725-1.OVGvNY&refcode=em-20260725-1&t=1&akid=1658%2E1086043%2EOrM_r6)
Peter -- This is remarkable: **_Fox News (yes, Fox News),_ moved Ohio’s Senate race to a “Toss-Up,” increasing our chances of flipping this seat!**
[****](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260725-1.OVGvNY&refcode=em20260725-1658&%3Bamount=5&t=2&akid=1658%2E1086043%2EOrM_r6)
What we’re building here in Ohio is special, and even _Fox News_ can’t ignore it.
Our momentum is growing by the day -- but so is the target on our backs. Republicans see that we have a clear path to victory, and they’re going to do everything in their power to stop us in our tracks. **[Before I say more, will you split $5 between my campaign and Wes Moore now so we can hit our $200,000 rapid-response goal and take on whatever comes next?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260725-1.OVGvNY&refcode=em-20260725-1&t=3&akid=1658%2E1086043%2EOrM_r6)**
In the first public poll of the general election, Fox News showed us 8 points ahead of Republican Jon Husted. **_That’s me, 8 points ahead, in a state Trump won by 11 points last time._ That’s a huge deal.**
Now, with today’s race ratings change, the momentum continues to shift in our favor.
**But here’s the problem:** You can bet that National Republicans are panicking. GOP dark-money groups were already pouring $133 million into this race to defeat me, and now that they’re looking to save face -- along with this crucial battleground seat -- they’ll be flooding this race with even more.
**I am their #1 target on the map this November because what happens here will decide Senate control.**
Look, Peter -- I don’t know what’s coming next, but I do know that the only way we can keep things going in our favor is by responding quickly in moments like this and fighting hard each and every day until the election. **Ohio broke the record for the most expensive Senate race in history last time, so we need a lot of support if we’re going to pull this off.**
**[That’s why I’m urgently asking: Will you split $5 right now between my campaign and Wes Moore to help us reach our critical rapid-response goal, flip this seat in Ohio, and take back the Senate majority?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260725-1.OVGvNY&refcode=em-20260725-1&t=4&akid=1658%2E1086043%2EOrM_r6)**

Every dollar counts and means a ton to me personally. Thank you so much.
Sherrod Brown

subject: “Fighting Loneliness”
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Powered by People, [poweredxpeople
body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240975%2E444211%2EWVWN6G)
I feel incredibly lucky to help lead Powered by People as a full time volunteer because I get to be part of something that is changing what’s possible in Texas.
It’s not just that our relational registration program is bringing in tens of thousands of new voters and dramatically improving the likelihood that they’ll vote (79% vs. 39%), it’s that we are also building an organizing army of thousands of people who are devoting their time and energy to saving this country through the tough work of meeting voters where they are in person and helping them vote.
These Powered by People volunteers have made a community from perfect strangers who now work shoulder to shoulder in common cause. They’re providing the answer to the unique challenge of our time: the isolation and division that is a product of social media algorithms and cynical politics that prioritizes technology and money over human connection and understanding.
I’ve thought that our slogan could be “Fighting Loneliness” — because that’s really what we’re doing.
As everyday Americans step up to volunteer with us, as they train with other new volunteers to learn our program and get certified as Volunteer Deputy Registrars, as they join together on college campuses, at concerts, at clubs and coffee shops to reach, register and personally stay in touch with the voters who are the margin of victory in Texas, they’re connecting with their fellow citizens and neighbors, they’re establishing real relationships face-to-face, and they’re doing the work that defines a democracy... a government of, by and for the people.
All of this is possible because of people like you who donate to ensure we have what it takes to not only keep this going but to expand it to reach even more voters and future voters. Not only can we win elections this way, we can change how politics works in Texas and maybe even the country. Defining ourselves not by our differences but in what we have in common, what we are able to accomplish together.
Thank you for giving us the chance to do this.
Beto

Vote by August 4
Voting ends Tuesday, August 4 at 7:00 PM. Do not wait to help us reach one more voter.
---
Final countdown to voting
August 4 is almost here. Vote Dr. Nila Devanath for Congress.
The clock is running. Every call, text, door knock, donation, and reminder can move one more voter before voting ends.
Dear Friend,
We are in the final countdown in Virginia’s 2nd District. Support alone is not enough now - we need action, turnout, and a final push from everyone who believes in this campaign.
I’m voting for **Dr. Nila Devanath** , and I hope you will too. She is a physician, attorney, mother, and advocate who understands the real challenges facing working families, veterans, students, and communities across VA-02.
Before voting ends, please do three things: make your voting plan, remind at least 10 people, and help Team Nila reach voters who still need to hear from us.

| Watch and share Help Dr. Nila reach more voters.

Dr. Nila is running a people-powered campaign. Now we need people-powered turnout.
Dr. Nila grew up here in Hampton Roads and has dedicated her career to public service, healthcare, policy, and standing up for people who too often get left behind. The difference now is turnout - who votes, who reminds a neighbor, and who helps us finish strong.
| **She fights for lower costs for working families.**
Dr. Nila believes billionaires and corporations should pay their fair share while families get relief.
---
**She is fighting for universal healthcare.**
As a doctor, she knows families should be able to get the care they need without being crushed by cost.
**She does not take corporate PAC money.**
This campaign is powered by people — not corporate special interests.
**She can make history.**
Dr. Nila has the chance to bring a much-needed new perspective to Congress and inspire the turnout needed to win.
| Take action now Do not wait. Help GOTV today.

This is personal for me. I grew up in Cincinnati. It's my hometown - the place that shaped everything I believe about America. My parents immigrated here with almost nothing, but they built a life because America was a nation of laws. A place where hard work was rewarded and the rules applied to everyone equally. So it cut deep when Cincinnati declared itself a sanctuary city. Think about the dangerous precedent that it sets. A local government openly standing up and saying: We will choose which federal laws we want to obey. If the government itself refuses to respect the law, why should anyone else? [This isn't a minor policy debate. This is the very fabric of our republic unraveling. An open border is not a border. A sanctuary city is actively rejecting the nation it sits in.](http://links.magaallies.com/u/click?_t=ec6977da27e4463794af691eb6b01adc&_m=a73cbed3c64b407497cb6f390f1c6edd&_e=opK-icTkvwtnhTxzy4U1Ti9XHPCW-pGKKo5v14BgpXgvECQVWaaYUQ-e_se5EFwK9AbBpuKWG1dret_7byh0GkuX8zCaEtPQAli9BxlLVlb39eDm-tWOxBTSt6j7cv36KfNk7RvmYOJWdF3nF8O3KF32U2oZ4cUr-HUOGM7gT2wnNV6H_QOgMfu-G-g2t-3qinkvlM52aqyVCOwpIaONn-QpsKpHUDgV4r1l97FCYfWwYvQCjNVlWWnoN09tuB5e_Pf53PGKa9auxXe8efKJhoOYDqRn-ke0-EYJOs_bHsF4Nx1m1hLUDe_pwHbXLhnmltvbFEjrXa3_1qFZESm74yT3bk8wCsOBcKofUmAjpXiPlxfJETlhFn2Fckqm327_pYfa6YfqTVz6ipwlF3YeLzscU890_KO2McBOH2e6gbVIKePoN1804qP61P6ajn6sCcefyW-fMQc6T_TQuSTpwKxVI_erdVBE9XyfioTxnvZFkuNxAEwI-CC4uySDUkJHjIzMF6YauHDT4fSE_9lvrCffYAhBmgYGlk7ZzY_4AuAV6u8E7-pYem8Koki8wPoX7BZELgzWKshJ8UljjzyiCvYIzMZerwBaQuhyTehBvtAkn__xLM8C2YSo_5qUbfJRIAXUyhM3D1ATQXWv4-6oJdsz50a3YwdTDNoe6V-cQ-acJ8o-cftdAVwHudN_bmVR5mO0GQ4DNYCOy3PX59HgzNBiQgVCsSdNVeRqM14Dsxk%3D) When you pick and choose which laws matter, you don't get a more compassionate society. clean_body: This isn't a minor policy debate. | I want your opinion. Should cities be allowed to ignore federal immigration law and declare themselves sanctuary cities? | This is personal for me. I grew up in Cincinnati. It's my hometown - the place that shaped everything I believe about America. My parents immigrated here with almost nothing, but they built a life because America was a nation of laws. A place where hard work was rewarded and the rules applied to everyone equally. So it cut deep when Cincinnati declared itself a sanctuary city. Think about the dangerous precedent that it sets. A local government openly standing up and saying: We will choose which federal laws we want to obey. If the government itself refuses to respect the law, why should anyone else? When you pick and choose which laws matter, you don't get a more compassionate society. You get crime. You get chaos. You get a total collapse of public trust. With summer in full swing and the campaign trail heating up, our team is facing an uphill battle against well-funded opponents who want to undo all of the progress we’ve made.
---
| [SUPPORT JEN KIGGANS](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._B50RExpfUvS6w)

Keeping our momentum going through the busy summer months means growing our team and expanding our outreach across the entire district. In the Navy, we know that no one accomplishes a mission by themselves, and the same is true on the campaign trail.

July 25, 2026
When AOC (Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez) posted, Dan Miressi agreed. The real issue isn't one vote on the NDAA (National Defense Authorization Act)--it's whether Connecticut deserves a representative who leads with independent judgment instead of following social media narratives. Connecticut needs a leader not just another follower. We already have five followers in the CT Congressional flock.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7e42a903-d021-4379-a13a-78318eab7078?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
When Miressi, a Republican candidate, adopts the same misleading narrative as Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez - Republican voters should ask which party Miressi is aligned with - or is he simply following the Democratic flock.
When someone runs for Congress, the public has a right to expect one basic qualification: **read the legislation before announcing how you would vote.**
That should be the minimum standard.
Yet Republican congressional candidate challenger **Dan Miressi** recently echoed Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's opposition to the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), posting simply: **" Nay vote as well."**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d85d268f-e485-4958-be20-76305049cb2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The problem is that AOC's central claim--that the NDAA would somehow "**merge parts of our military with the IDF (Israel Defense Force)** "--is simply not what the legislation says.
## **What Section 224 Actually Does**
Section 224 of the NDAA establishes the **United States -Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative.**
It directs the Secretary of Defense to designate an executive agent responsible for coordinating cooperation between the United States and Israel in:
* Defense technology research
* Development
* Testing
* Evaluation
* Integration
* Industrial cooperation

* **Nothing in the legislation merges the United States Armed Forces with the Israel Defense Forces.**
* **Nothing places American troops under Israeli command.**
* **Nothing places Israeli troops under American command.**
* **Nothing creates a combined military.**

Instead, it strengthens defense technology cooperation between two longstanding allies, much like the United States cooperates with numerous allied nations on intelligence, weapons development, cybersecurity, missile defense, and military exercises.
**** But Republican Congressman Mike Lawler in responding to AOC states:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a782cd67-5980-4fc2-b413-3cbb79a21665?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Congressman **Mike Lawler** responded directly to AOC's claim.
He pointed out the obvious:
America regularly cooperates with allies through intelligence sharing, joint military exercises, defense technology, and weapons development.
That does **not** mean America is "merging" its military with another country's armed forces.
Lawler correctly called the accusation what it was--a false characterization of the legislation.
**Unfortunately, Dan Miressi chose to repeat AOC 's conclusion rather than examine the bill itself.**
## **Congress Requires More Than Social Media**
Miressi's response raises a simple but important question:
**Did he actually read the legislation?**
Members of Congress vote on thousands of pages of legislation affecting national security, healthcare, taxation, energy policy, and the economy.
**The job requires careful review --not reacting to social media.**
Whether someone ultimately supports or opposes Section 224 is a legitimate policy debate.
But that debate should begin with what the bill actually says--not what goes viral on X.
**Candidates should lead with facts.**
Instead, Miressi appeared willing to accept AOC's description without independently reviewing the legislation. Would he follow her blindly if he was a Congressman just because she tweets first without analysis?
That is not the level of preparation Connecticut deserves.
## **The Goldstein Contrast**
The contrast with **Dr. Michael Goldstein** could not be clearer.
Goldstein supports America's strategic alliance with Israel because he believes it serves **American national security interests** , not because of political pressure or campaign contributions.
Importantly, **Dr. Goldstein has not received support from AIPAC, has not received contributions from AIPAC-related PACs, and has not even been approached by AIPAC regarding his congressional campaign.**
His support for Israel is based entirely upon his own judgment.
That is significant because critics frequently attempt to dismiss pro-Israel positions by claiming elected officials are motivated by PAC money.
That argument simply does not apply to Michael Goldstein.
His views are independent.
## **Connecticut Republicans Deserve Better**
Republican primary voters should expect candidates who:
* Read legislation before commenting on it.
* Think independently.
* Verify facts before repeating talking points.
* Understand national security.
* Exercise independent judgment.

Instead, Dan Miressi chose to repeat one of AOC's most misleading claims regarding the NDAA.
That should concern Republican voters.
## **The Bottom Line**
This election is about far more than one section of one bill.
It is about judgment.
Congress should be filled with representatives who study legislation instead of reposting headlines, who think independently instead of following social-media trends, and who put facts ahead of political theater.
_**Dr. Michael Goldstein has not been supported by AIPAC. He has not been approached by AIPAC. He has not based his positions on political contributions.**_
His support for the U.S.-Israel alliance comes from his own assessment of America's national security interests and his belief that strong democratic allies make America safer.
Connecticut deserves representatives who **read the bill before casting the vote** --not candidates who let someone else do the reading for them.
_**That is why voters should go to the polls on August 11th with early voting August 3-9 to vote for Michael Goldstein the Republican endorsed candidate in the Republican primary.**_

The second-quarter fundraising numbers are official now, and I want you to see them — because they say just about everything about the two campaigns in this race.
Here's mine: more than 10,000 people chipped in last quarter. 91% of them gave $100 or less, and our average donation was just $15. More than a quarter gave more than once. Together, you helped us out-raise my opponent more than two to one — $1.6 million to his $742,000.
That's not a number I take for granted. That's a movement of working people giving what they can.
Now here's his: nearly half of everything John Braun raised last quarter — 49.7% — came from the national Republican machine. Committees tied to D.C. party bosses. PACs backed by corporations, special interests, and the political elite.
His support from actual people in Southwest Washington has been shrinking for three quarters straight. When the checks from home dried up, the D.C. machine threw him a rope.
That tells you exactly who he'd answer to in Congress. And it tells you exactly who I answer to: you.
I don't take a dime of corporate PAC money — I never have. This campaign only works if people like you keep it going, and with more than $3.9 million banked for the fight ahead, we have real momentum.
Maybe add something about 7 mil reserved against us in TV....
Let's build on it. Will you chip in $5 and keep this a campaign powered by working Washingtonians — not the highest bidder? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]

Thank you for standing with me.

The GOP’s eight-figure attack ad buys are working, and we need your help to fight back immediately.

Peter, our narrow lead in this Senate race is shrinking:
| | **Cooper (D)** | **Whatley (R)** | **Cooper Edge**
---|---|---|---
**June 2026** | 50% | 43% | ****\+ 7****
**July 2026** | 48% | 44% | ****\+ 4****
**In just a month, our polling advantage has been cut by almost HALF.**
The GOP’s eight-figure attack ad buys are working, and we need your help to fight back immediately. Even just a few bucks will be a huge help. If you’re able and willing to chip in, please use the link below:
[**_https:/secure.actblue.com/cooper/email_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/17141?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk840&amount=5&t=8&akid=2319%2E124072%2Exux5YA)
This new poll should be a wake-up call for Democrats everywhere.
We need to flip North Carolina to have any shot at taking back the Senate. There’s so much riding on this race, and unless we respond to these tightening polls, **there’s a very real chance Republicans could hold this seat and stay in control of the Senate until 2029.**
That’s why we just launched a new ad to reach folks all across North Carolina with our message – and right now, we're relying on your grassroots support to keep it running.
The GOP is trying to drown us out in nearly $100 million worth of attack ads (so far), and whether we’re able to respond and overcome them depends on getting our message in front of as many people as possible. **Every voter we reach and every dollar we raise makes a real difference in a race that will be decided by a razor-thin margin.**

clean_body: I am ready to win this Special Election, but I need your help. | Fellow Patriot, With less than three weeks to go, The legacy my brother, Lindsey, built can never be replicated, but I can honor him by working as hard as he did, every single day, for the people of South Carolina. Last week, President Trump encouraged me to run in the upcoming Senate Special Election by saying: "Run, Darline, Run!" That endorsement isn't just an honor. It's a call to action. The President knows South Carolina needs a fighter who will finish what my brother started, and he's counting on us to deliver. I intend to earn every vote because that's what this job demands, and that's what South Carolina deserves. But here's the truth: My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years stockpiling campaign cash. I'm new to this. The Special Election Primary is August 11th - just 17 days away. Every dollar raised between now and then determines whether we can compete on the airwaves, get out the vote, and win. There is no "catching up later." This is the moment. President Trump believes in this campaign. Thank you, Darline Graham United States Senator (R-SC) | | Paid for by Darline for Senate Don't want to receive any more of our emails? Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, speaks in a protest march towards Parliament from Jantar Mantar on July 20, 2026 in New Delhi, India. Photo by Sanchit Khanna/Hindustan Times via Getty Images.
DELHI--Protesters occupying the central parts of Delhi, India were triumphant on Saturday evening after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government accepted all demands raised by the movement's leaders, including the resignation of the country's education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
The protest was spearheaded by the newly formed Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)--a wordplay on Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The word "cockroach" is attributed to the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, who in May referred to the youth of the country as "cockroaches" during a court hearing.
Ministers of the Modi government's cabinet sat for talks with CJP representatives on Friday and Saturday. At the end of the talks on Saturday, the CJP announced that the government had agreed to all their demands.
Accepting all the protesters' demands was a rare surrender to popular dissent in Modi's 12 years of being in power, during which the Hindu nationalist leader has built his image as a strongman that does not back down or take criticism kindly.
"This is just the beginning of a larger movement that will restore basic governance and will work for the people of this country," said Sauraav Das, a spokesperson for CJP.
Hundreds of thousands of these cockroach protesters had been assembling for over a month at Jantar Mantar, which is less than half a mile south of Connaught Place, the central market in the heart of Delhi. They were demanding the resignation of Pradhan, who is also a senior leader in India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party, the party of Modi. The protesters at Jantar Mantar consider Pradhan to be responsible for failing to prevent "paper leaks"--the unauthorized release of highly competitive national college entrance examinations, often hours and sometimes minutes before the exam is due.
The Jantar Mantar movement emerged in May in response to a leak of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET), the countrywide medical entrance exam. Reports suggest at least a dozen students across the country died by suicide after the tests were canceled. Protesters claim the number is over 20. The protestor's demand that the families of each of these students be paid ten million Indian rupees was accepted by the government on Saturday.
After Delhi's police and other armed forces cracked down heavily against protesters on Monday, the market became a pale shadow of its usual self. Traffic was redirected. And at least half a dozen metro stations around it were shut. Instead it was full with a young, Gen Z crowd who were there to register their dissent against the Modi government in growing numbers and spirit unseen in recent years.
Betu Yadav, a 26-year-old post-graduate student from Uttar Pradesh was hit on the back of her head with batons by male police officers on Monday, leading to intense bleeding that required seven stitches. As news of the government agreeing to the demands emerged, Yadav, still wearing a bandage over her head, said that she can finally celebrate the fruit of her month-long struggle.
"The fight that we fought has transformed into a big success. And today, on the 25th of July, Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned. Along with the resignation of Pradhan, the struggle to overthrow the BJP government will also be achieved by the same youth and the same crowd," she said.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/27171362-d05c-4e0b-add5-0c9df7077af7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Crowds of supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party gather at Jantar Mantar to Join the ongoing protest, on July 23, 2026 in New Delhi, India. Photo by Vipin Kumar/Hindustan Times via Getty Images.
## Police Brutality Backfired
Many of the Cockroach protesters had poured into Jantar Mantar from various parts of the country since Monday, when leaders of CJP called for a protest march to the Indian parliament demanding Pradhan's resignation.
As protesters began their march on parliament, the Delhi Police and other armed forces cracked down heavily, jamming the internet in central Delhi, using tear gas, beating students with batons, and in some instances shooting them with pellet guns. At least one person has been [reportedly](https://substack.com/redirect/5cb005eb-3297-4ab3-84b5-c11a33a2513e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) left with a permanent disability due to the use of pellet guns.
Multiple students were detained, many of whom have been since released and charges were pressed against some.
"I was shoved to the ground and pulled across," said Sachin Rawat, a software engineer who came from Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. Rawat incurred injuries on his forehead, shoulder, arm, and legs on Monday. "I consider this as the love of Delhi Police," he said satirically, adding, "whenever there is a revolutionary struggle, there will be such signs of it being repressed."
Video evidence has since gone viral on social media showing a senior police officer slapping a young woman, and other male officers groping and attacking women.
The brutalities witnessed on Monday pushed more students to join the movement, with lines to enter the central area of the protest site reaching several blocks at any point of the day in the past week. Since videos of police action against students went viral on social media, protests [spread](https://substack.com/redirect/def699e8-2e65-44c9-a1f0-8810f9b4abc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to a dozen other cities around the country.
Apart from Pradhan's resignation, the leaders of the CJP also demanded that all charges pressed against peaceful protesters be withdrawn. A spokesperson for CJP who was present at talks said that the government has agreed to withdraw all charges against protesters across the country.
## A Broken Education System
"I had to appear twice for the same exam. It was really stressful. I still don't know which university I will be admitted to," said 17-year-old Mohammad Kashan, whose dream is to study at the prestigious Jawaharlal Nehru University in Delhi. Earlier this year, Kashan had taken the Central University Examination Test (CUET), which admits students into federal government-owned colleges across the country. Each year, over ten million students appear for this exam.
Kashan came to Delhi with a friend on July 22, on a low-cost train ticket from Patna, the capital city of Bihar, a state in eastern India. Kashan said the police brutality against students he saw on social media for simply demanding accountability pushed him to join the protests. He has no friends or family in Delhi and was sleeping on the sidewalk since he arrived with a thin cloth for a bed and his back-pack as a pillow.
Twenty-one-year-old Shalu Yadav also took a train but traveled even further, from Hyderabad, in the southern Indian state of Telangana. She is studying law and said she fought with her parents to be present at the protest.
"Our education system is completely broken, it does not guarantee a seat in an institute nor does it guarantee a job. I saw the call for the protest and I decided I need to attend it," Yadav said.
Since Modi took office in 2014, the budget of India's Ministry of Education, as a share of the national budget, has dropped by nearly half, even as overall spending has increased, according to a recent [investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/e7a37f58-bd74-48c0-b8f3-6c06903b68ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by The Indian Express.
Protesters pointed out that the government is instead privatizing education rapidly. "The entire exam system gets outsourced to private contractors. So there is no accountability for paper leaks. Funding for universities and research has been cut down. We are against this entire education policy," said Priyam, a master's student at Delhi University and a member of Collective, a progressive students group.
"This is bigger than a protest, it is a movement. There is no future in this country right now. I won't leave till the government resolves our issues, including the resignation of the education minister," Yadav said on Thursday.
Many like Yadav are now packing their bags to finally head home after a week, or in some cases after almost a month, of volunteering at the protest site.
## Solidarity with Students of Gaza
For 21-year-old Tubassum, a Master's student at Delhi University, the movement symbolizes solidarity with other struggles. Although she has two cousins who had to re-appear for the medical tests and were depressed through the entire ordeal, showing up for a protest means a lot more for Tubassum, who came sporting a keffiyeh over her burqa. She was in ninth grade when her mother and aunts joined the Muslim women's protest at Shaheen Bagh, Delhi, in 2019-20, against a citizenship bill that discriminated against Muslims.
"I remember how people showed up for each other in 2019 at Shaheen Bagh against the Modi government. I want to extend the same solidarity to my peers. And while we raise our voice for our education, I also stand with the students of Gaza who suffered a genocide. Whose education has been ripped due to the genocide" she said.
The Modi government, which has systemically targeted Indian Muslims through [immigration laws](https://substack.com/redirect/eeeb1c44-8660-4804-b3d8-75654cc2b1c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [regulating food habits](https://substack.com/redirect/eeeb1c44-8660-4804-b3d8-75654cc2b1c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [revising voter rolls](https://substack.com/redirect/e9662214-047e-4017-8325-44bd6b1f6c57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), is one of Israel's staunchest [allies](https://substack.com/redirect/e9423344-ba61-4b17-832e-a8cbb9040181?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Bhumi, an undergraduate student at Delhi's Ambedkar University, and a member of Collective, a progressive student group, was also wearing a keffiyeh and has been attending the protest since last month. "No one is free until everyone is free. This struggle is not only about education but also about basic rights. Not only about paper leaks, but also about rights of workers, farmers, and transpeople. And this solidarity extends to Gaza," she said.

## Modi Loses the Narrative
While the central demand of the Jantar Mantar movement was the resignation of the education minister, protesters did not hesitate to direct their attention at Modi.
Since Monday's police action, the most popular slogan heard through the protest site chanted in Hindi translates to, "Whenever Modi gets scared, he sends the police in front." Gen Z protesters speaking the language of viral Instagram reels and memes were also often heard chanting nasty slogans that ridicule Modi.
"We cannot forget that the ruling party BJP is responsible for this. We cannot forget that Home Minister Amit Shah is responsible for the brutalities. We cannot forget that this is ultimately Narendra Modi's government that perpetrated the paper leaks and the police brutality," said Neha Bora, national president of the leftist group All India Students Association, during a speech from the center stage of the protest site on Thursday night. Bora went on a hunger strike for 23 days, ending on July 20, demanding the resignation of the education minister.
In response, Modi has promised to set up fast track courts that address the paper leak issue. On Thursday night, he released a statement in a vertical [video](https://substack.com/redirect/0ef023a8-61d8-43c2-aa2e-fd218f57deb0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) format on his social media--seen as a way to be more Gen Z friendly--promising that his government will take imminent action against paper leaks. On Friday night there was another video with a similar message. And on Saturday, his government bowed down to the demands.
Rahul Verma, an election analyst and a professor of politics at Shiv Nadar University, argues that many from within Modi's Hindu nationalist base also appeared to support the movement, placing him on the defensive.
"Unlike many previous mobilisations against the BJP this movement draws hugely from groups that have constituted an important part of the party's electoral coalition," he wrote in a [column](https://substack.com/redirect/43b1d06d-e7b7-46f8-950a-95be387406b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "A large number of these young, aspirational Indians and their parents on the protest site may have even voted for BJP in the recent past. They are protesting because the systems through which they hoped to advance appear increasingly unreliable."

Ministers of the Modi government's cabinet sat for talks with CJP representatives on Friday and Saturday. At the end of the talks on Saturday, the CJP announced that the government had agreed to all their demands. Accepting all the protesters' demands was a rare surrender to popular dissent in Modi's 12 years of being in power, during which the Hindu nationalist leader has built his image as a strongman that does not back down or take criticism kindly. They were demanding the resignation of Pradhan, who is also a senior leader in India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party, the party of Modi. It’s difficult to admit that I can't do this alone. [**There's so much weighing on me right now, and finding the right words feels impossible. Working cows and driving tractors growing up made me who I am today. It taught me the value of hard work, the importance of keeping your word, and what it means to sacrifice for something bigger than yourself. Trust me, I know all the constant emails and texts can weigh on you. It wears on me too. Some days I wonder if it's worth it. But then I remember why I'm here. I didn't come to Washington because I love asking true patriots like you for money. I didn't run for Congress at 29 years old to become the youngest House Republican so I could spend my nights begging for donations. I came because my kids deserve to grow up in a better America than I grew up in — and right now, that's not guaranteed. Being a husband and a father are the two most important things in my life. Sometimes, when I'm holding my kids, I feel like I'm holding the whole world in my arms. They're everything to me. They're the wind in my sails when it comes to the mission I've committed my life and career to. And at the end of my life, I want to sit before the Father Almighty and declare that I did all I could to leave this great country better off than it was when I grew up. I refuse to look my kids in the eye someday and tell them I gave up when it mattered most. [**That's why I'm still here. That's why I keep sending these messages.**](http://links.conservativeum.com/s/c/L0Wz4kU6x1Lt4pNkCugdX5w6IcNzT37y1wRtYCJozWmSNXvcviiA_mKEEFirRRauUKkxE2eZx9YzWKbQnugIVnCV2OgY_lj7S_x55X6YL2A1ksBdN0sh4TwVA3DXZ-qiM3pttV2Vuzml1zfHmKKnfASPupiSXCLYNMCCrRY_TKinDwWr3UaRcJrcdWSIbAEUcJC6E0jmHECERAu1Vkpb7-R-hyK9NjHfZ9M-cD3VBHvdTw0C7DKV7KzoHXdlWb6saDqox8-7hDA5pDTMp7bFc_reUftiHX3bO5OPSUz87UTouRWb-U6Yn7pyjz0oCF4YhEg8zobaw9n_ClqAvFfLGSF2TF_LMR_QmJUhb0N_ykJ63Vk7GkWPkdDwzjWFbYys2_OKLr64YeBiDikz9NoEeh5SRS4G-4o1vPe8s54JGfLXyk3UVrpVMzOK9-j4YFhOiAgs6aqfMaMXYJvacE6jU2eNM77nwYnSCkoN3k5eLlHK18RvAnss_O9YDJ4l3Coe8a8Wft2MrR6DysE04Jq7xVht4wh74Ug-ZTkTESiwL4powu9n2zbJ3CQxiU-XrMrfLvD1ljytU40upj8VcVSxzNKwHMnTct-ogeoTtRaFTmuZSViSKeoESIirO2Lk-u9HZ6rJz9saXH-9PNwHFMc2I-hIXFYOSxorLOrjdLmaXz-v6qHDHXnE7NR6i_8BxkbsMnlchdV-Zb12KzhY1JqP8Iu1ErN_9Q8d-AE68tj6cpGNkWVbDhwLH_-QpDRd1KY1AN7VsMKqMLEJhzEx0lIMuSvgOvYnRpOvvMv92nNwdENYTVo/cFptyLgT3g9j-JeFEpQqNihCwo3k2bOY/23) Because nothing — I repeat — nothing is more important to me than fighting off the vicious leftist attacks against the soul of our country. On Wednesday, we called on the Rules and Bylaws Committee to put South Carolina and Nevada first, because no Democrat wins the White House without Black, Latino, and AAPI voters, and no nominee should be chosen without hearing from them first. Yesterday, the Committee did exactly that. We thank the members of the Committee for getting this right.
> "The contrast could not be clearer. While Republicans work to silence Black voters after gutting the Voting Rights Act, Democrats just voted to put Black voters at the very front of the process of picking a president. That is more than symbolism. It means candidates will build their campaigns, their platforms, and their coalitions around our communities from day one.
> "The work isn't finished. The full DNC meets in Austin next month to ratify this calendar, and The Collective PAC urges every DNC member to vote yes. Then comes the real test: matching this calendar with real investment in the organizers, the candidates, and the infrastructure in these communities. We've spent ten years building Black political power, and we intend to make sure the voters who go first in 2028 are also funded first."
For a decade, The Collective PAC has worked to build Black political power, helping elect more than 500 candidates, raising over $50 million, and training more than 2,000 operatives across the country.
The full DNC is expected to ratify the 2028 calendar at its August meeting. The Collective PAC urges Rules and Bylaws Committee members to send forward a calendar that puts South Carolina and Nevada first.

The Collective PAC is the nation's largest political action committee dedicated to building Black political power and increasing Black representation at all levels of government. Peter,

In June, The Wall Street Journal reported that the establishment schemed
to narrow Michigan’s Democratic primary candidate field in hopes of
defeating our campaign, because in their eyes, I’m “dangerous.”

Just a few weeks later, the field really did narrow to us vs. their
preferred candidate, Haley Stevens.

Here’s what I think of being called “dangerous.”

If you're the establishment, I'm dangerous.
If you're AIPAC, I'm dangerous.
If you're a corporate PAC, I'm pretty damn dangerous.

But to the working people of Michigan? Hell no.

Peter, I've never
taken a dime from a corporate PAC, and I never will.

I wrote the book on Medicare for All because I believe healthcare is a
right, not a line item on a billionaire’s earnings call.

I've spent my career going after the people who profit off making life
harder for working people, and I'm not about to stop now that I'm this
close to the U.S. Senate.

That's exactly why the establishment, AIPAC, and corporate PACs are
spending so much to stop us.

They’re betting we run out of steam, but I’m betting on this grassroots
team — and I really like our odds.

And their families, well, they make sacrifices every day to support their loved ones. But so often when our veterans come home from their service, they’re met with a system that doesn’t always honor their sacrifice. Our veterans face barriers to health care, benefits, and the support they need. This is not the thanks that they deserve. Something needs to change. Congress has a responsibility to provide veterans with the physical, mental, and financial assistance they need after returning home. That’s why I’m doing something about it. I’ve consistently fought to fix the system by expanding veterans’ health care, supporting mental health services, and helping servicemembers transition to civilian life. name: True the Vote
subject: Doors Are Opening. Enter the antagonists.
body:
July 25, 2026 | Read Online ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/v8ugklp2w3trhvwkqn9fghvz2qo8ec9h0lxm2/p8heh9h4nl5ez7tqh3/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2IvMzh1cGhraDJwZGtxNXQzN3h4bDc1ZjQ1bDd4MjRoN2h6eGczbQ== )

From Catherine
--------------

Hi Friend —

Something is different this week. You can feel the shift.

For years we said the same thing to the same closed doors. Our elections are riddled with process problems, which make them vulnerable to fraud. The records will show it, if anyone will only look. And for years the answer came back as a shrug, empty promises, hollow press releases, another door closing.

This week, doors are opening. Let's start with the rolls, because that is where all of this started for True the Vote back in the day.

Twenty-five states are now running sixty-eight million registrations through the SAVE database, flagging more than 480,000 questionable records in just ten states, so the numbers will continue to climb. And that is from a fairly narrow look. The real number of bad records, if ever exposed through a comprehensive audit, would be exponentially higher. But it is a good start.

Enter the antagonists. Four states — California, New Jersey, Nevada, Pennsylvania — refuse to run a SAVE check at all. Homeland Security estimates over 250,000 noncitizen registrations would be found sitting on their rolls. Of course, those four states say the DHS numbers can't be trusted.

Then, on July 21, the Governor of New Jersey reluctantly admitted that 6,600 noncitizens had been added to the state's rolls and that four hundred of them had voted — but insisted it was a software glitch. The company that wrote the software says her state's own process approved them, and based on our information, we side with the vendor. The process itself is what's broken. The software just digitized it.

The argument at the center of this debacle is the reliability of the SAVE database. SAVE was originally designed to check eligibility for social service benefits, not for voting. But it does contain data useful in determining citizenship status, which is what informs voting eligibility.

So we are told that SAVE sometimes returns a bad match, and therefore all checking should stop. Think of it. What business closes its books because the ledger didn't balance on the first pass? A flagged record is a question, not a verdict. To refuse to look is not caution. It is a way of choosing not to know. Cleaning up the rolls is bookkeeping. It is not a millstone to hang around a voter's neck, and it is not — for crying out loud — a scheme to keep anyone from voting. Either a person qualifies to vote or they don't.

Which brings us to a reality check, because the real work, if it is to be done, can’t start in databases at all. It has to start in us. In two years, confidence that our elections are run fairly and accurately has fallen off a cliff, from 76% down to 66% nationwide. And 83% of us want voter ID. Americans want common sense reforms.

And it's not about just citizenship checks, or ID, or basic record accuracy, or mail ballots, or month long voting, or machines, or foreign influence, its about all of it.

Confidence in elections will not be won back by political arguments. It will be won back by good housekeeping and practical improvements in our processes. The reason politicians can't make this a pitch for common sense is that they are conditioned to saber-rattling. How wonderful would it be to see fear traded for hopeful leadership that actually solves simple problems. And this really is simple, which is why it's so maddening. But even the admission from Governor Sherrill is progress.

Change is happening. We just can't quit.

A few more things. Our team has recently gone back deep into the Georgia election records (on a matter that has nothing to do with citizenship checks), and what we're seeing is stunning — but it’s data-heavy and could be confusing, so we're working right now on a way to help tell the story clearly, with receipts. Very exciting. And Trapped (Detroit) — years of work, thousands of hours, exposing the human cost of vote fraud — is nearly finished. We're looking at an end-of-month release for the trailer and the accompanying new websites.

None of this is a finish line, we know that. But doors of all types are opening. We are moving, and not just in circles. The journey is changing course. And we're here for it.

Keep the faith. Never quit. Ephesians 6 FTW!

Hi there, it’s Nancy Lacore, the Democrat running to flip South Carolina’s First District.
I have a lot of thoughts about what’s been going on with Pete Hegseth.
Not only did he remove me from my position as Chief of the Navy Reserve after 35 years of service, but he’s actively undermining the foundation of our military.
Hegseth has fired more than a dozen senior military officers, including an Army chief of staff and two other generals who were ousted recently.
And now, he’s waging a war with Iran that could put our national security and countless American lives on the line.
That kind of behavior isn’t just destabilizing – it’s dangerous.
Now more than ever, we need leadership that’s rooted in honor, service, and respect. And that’s exactly why I’m running for Congress in South Carolina’s First District.
If we’re going to flip this seat and take back a Democratic House Majority, I need your help. Can you make a split donation of $25 or whatever you can, to Resist Reclaim Rebuild and my campaign? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-lacore]

While global tensions rise, the last thing we need is reckless leadership that’s willing to gamble with American lives.
We need steady, experienced leaders who are focused on delivering results – not inciting chaos, playing political games, and putting their own interests above the nation’s.
And I’m running for Congress to restore that kind of leadership – but we have a long road ahead of us to flip this seat and restore some accountability to Washington.

body:
I joined Adam Sexton in the studio yesterday.

| |
---
| | Dear David, Yesterday, I sat down with Adam Sexton to record a television interview for WMUR. [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/as7dX5BUPwzgqiTiFt-fng~~/AAUS1hA~/2FL2P1MEMvcDOB7NGD_p9kl0oBnA7bFvM0XVfAZUlGYYTKAqjqa_hVw7HBVDQldtOu2nzGP1NdbsbFUa5UobenRny9g9eKA86A2l_mIVYcsv6t9UPhs9J3XEdXTHuZF-BSyltAUqkw5pUWoxFnkDj-Z-dD-c89J5BHEJNEYGBDD88q93NdKLBRtqh3vfBsJk150OKSJN3oOe30kldtQ1tWQJi99esVwow8Fzoc4EO42td6rVdD2m-_14OgJW0U5m) **[If you’d like to check it out, it’s airing at 10:30 AM tomorrow on WMUR! You can watch a brief trailer and pitch in to support my campaign at the link below.](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/as7dX5BUPwzgqiTiFt-fng~~/AAUS1hA~/2FL2P1MEMvcDOB7NGD_p9kl0oBnA7bFvM0XVfAZUlGYYTKAqjqa_hVw7HBVDQldtOu2nzGP1NdbsbFUa5UobenRny9g9eKA86A2l_mIVYcsv6t9UPhs9J3XEdXTHuZF-BSyltAUqkw5pUWoxFnkDj-Z-dD-c89J5BHEJNEYGBDD88q93NdKLBRtqh3vfBsJk150OKSJN3oOe30kldtQ1tWQJi99esVwow8Fzoc4EO42td6rVdD2m-_14OgJW0U5m)** | | [DONATE & WATCH](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/as7dX5BUPwzgqiTiFt-fng~~/AAUS1hA~/2FL2P1MEMvcDOB7NGD_p9kl0oBnA7bFvM0XVfAZUlGYYTKAqjqa_hVw7HBVDQldtOu2nzGP1NdbsbFUa5UobenRny9g9eKA86A2l_mIVYcsv6t9UPhs9J3XEdXTHuZF-BSyltAUqkw5pUWoxFnkDj-Z-dD-c89J5BHEJNEYGBDD88q93NdKLBRtqh3vfBsJk150OKSJN3oOe30kldtQ1tWQJi99esVwow8Fzoc4EO42td6rVdD2m-_14OgJW0U5m)
---
We talked about the DNC and New Hampshireʼs presidential primary, renewable energy, Social Security, the wars in Iran and Ukraine, and the rising dissatisfaction among voters when it comes to status quo politics and status quo politicians.
But at the end of the interview, Adam asked me something I wasn’t expecting. He asked if I was angry.
**The truth is that yes, David, I am angry.**
Iʼm angry that Donald Trump dragged us into a war that has killed 18 Americans, thousands of Iranians, and threatened the lives and livelihoods of people around the world.
Iʼm angry that ICE agents continue to terrorize and kill innocent people around the country and the Trump administration presses forward with their hateful “mass-deportation” agenda.
Iʼm angry that Republicans in Washington passed a bill last year that kicked millions of Americans off Medicaid and slashed funding for food assistance just so the rich can get richer.
I’m angry that our elected leaders spend more time cozying up to the rich and powerful and trying to go viral on social media than they do working to make things better for people.
**My anger is rooted in my recognition that none of this was inevitable. It fuels my conviction that we can organize with compassion and make better policy going forward if we keep the people we are fighting for at the center of everything we do.**

clean_body: I joined Adam Sexton in the studio yesterday. | | | | Dear David, Yesterday, I sat down with Adam Sexton to record a television interview for WMUR. | | We talked about the DNC and New Hampshireʼs presidential primary, renewable energy, Social Security, the wars in Iran and Ukraine, and the rising dissatisfaction among voters when it comes to status quo politics and status quo politicians. But at the end of the interview, Adam asked me something I wasn’t expecting. He asked if I was angry. The truth is that yes, David, I am angry. Iʼm angry that Donald Trump dragged us into a war that has killed 18 Americans, thousands of Iranians, and threatened the lives and livelihoods of people around the world. Iʼm angry that ICE agents continue to terrorize and kill innocent people around the country and the Trump administration presses forward with their hateful “mass-deportation” agenda. Iʼm angry that Republicans in Washington passed a bill last year that kicked millions of Americans off Medicaid and slashed funding for food assistance just so the rich can get richer. I’m angry that our elected leaders spend more time cozying up to the rich and powerful and trying to go viral on social media than they do working to make things better for people. My anger is rooted in my recognition that none of this was inevitable. It fuels my conviction that we can organize with compassion and make better policy going forward if we keep the people we are fighting for at the center of everything we do. She lost her parents. Traffickers see an opportunity.
Displaced children with nowhere to turn are exactly who traffickers target.

| | | | [](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=179e04179cee4d5e8553c80fd3ebfeeb&_e=KM9znROPViLnYRhZLW2zPVv661x_2xBp2iGChc9c1wms4U-oh46TFkQtcmByyoID_BlHOW05Euiv8eVcvwoYsyJOLZ9iIQTeHrD2h3X1qOQ8UeHyANDMoutCVqYUNdACCzRdj780rD7eLrWkdPfqGJTOFnvV2TTrtFYi4P_7G128eW0tnz1LVx61Lz811RVoqF2yN0-co4M4L7qq5IsA-hj87XXPp2OqmBhn69JrPvCw3K5XQmMNGeAeWailjBoo3X3-4vEsINrCpWBRpYhWJJ4JoKfV0atFpTZspUMUbxbU02doADXFC3fIo5qhd7pxDUR-VC-bluwaH9lFA8K4gImhV2LqRWfs8q2Wk2Q3v7anph_adx5QhO50wwf8XEFA-TbarYUx_2RGIWtFQF6k0njz56Ymc53V7OPP8Ifkf5yqZpK3FeVGXPjCP-Dh1I59PK3iZkRMIt8btD_Q6YuRhzQXWbcbXKN1D2qepXM2mpelArvM6HJ2kqyvMa5yTxfSMKNOh_pF4_8k0Ms8eqP2eO2oEdDLuRT_zzUGGRATl3Iu3Xuu_kKY5HmM7aR__vA9XyOnaTui1uhL1jeNl8aXwuL6iJ9TTg44qS6JXS1qGlJ9O1H5loWyZIeiNT94_ixB4DPizZUOQiC_Tx1rk4B9Jl_Gc2kPlxxsG9mPXbdTMPE3NEcE5sEEoxgIHzAGlPCk)

| |
---
| | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | | Friend, A child who survived the earthquake in Venezuela may have lost everything else.Their parents. Their home. Every relative who might have taken them in. Now they have nowhere to sleep, nothing to eat, and no one left to protect them.**When a child has nowhere to turn, someone else will offer to take her somewhere.** **Too often, that someone is a trafficker, and they know exactly how to make the offer sound like help. **
---
[](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=179e04179cee4d5e8553c80fd3ebfeeb&_e=KM9znROPViLnYRhZLW2zPVv661x_2xBp2iGChc9c1wms4U-oh46TFkQtcmByyoID_BlHOW05Euiv8eVcvwoYsyJOLZ9iIQTeHrD2h3X1qOQ8UeHyANDMoutCVqYUNdACCzRdj780rD7eLrWkdPfqGJTOFnvV2TTrtFYi4P_7G128eW0tnz1LVx61Lz811RVoqF2yN0-co4M4L7qq5IsA-hj87XXPp2OqmBhn69JrPvCw3K5XQmMNGeAeWailjBoohHOQw4cNr5s3Xe3FdVIN4Qs2QCg6lcJwckbWeTgSHH_n6_p4lYVPyjdacm-QySki3I34pFn-y009Q5Huk_Q3Jq9zreLKib3J_1YQscxuYa6Aa-5II1oT_oU_p1v9eqfap5nOeiWiYUTNhiiXwydwPVu7SH04TQJK8ID3Ui0o29PPDWkdSXiprTfhIu8Ic4ZgFtaih8bfQqBFQkN2qNUj8N_ZOfrlEgMn6AilNeo5MzkfhR4bHVBX-ZcLBQ5rUvGhF9j7aQR6V3uuWRcwqv8NgZvas-Yq0x7Q-bfw5T7rxeEzHTwadqZ6OAifUy3gE3F0iRTIlJZVKtHl5xf2YBUqGuQwbSS6q-Rwno_x2qXuYgkmt9YWGdB6S0gNXnlo4zu50xRD1J4mwPyl7FPtWJhOzzxxj9TllNZd6fgvAzLuRZjoMwBkt8DUCDZrTiO2C8Tv)

They study the gaps left behind by disaster, and they move quickly, often faster than the systems built to protect children can respond. A shelter without enough staff. A registration process that hasn't caught up. A crowd of frightened families too overwhelmed to watch every child closely. These are the openings traffickers are trained to find.
---
[ Give Before It's Too Late](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=179e04179cee4d5e8553c80fd3ebfeeb&_e=KM9znROPViLnYRhZLW2zPVv661x_2xBp2iGChc9c1wms4U-oh46TFkQtcmByyoID_BlHOW05Euiv8eVcvwoYsyJOLZ9iIQTeHrD2h3X1qOQ8UeHyANDMoutCVqYUNdACCzRdj780rD7eLrWkdPfqGJTOFnvV2TTrtFYi4P_7G128eW0tnz1LVx61Lz811RVoqF2yN0-co4M4L7qq5IsA-hj87XXPp2OqmBhn69JrPvCw3K5XQmMNGeAeWailjBoo5dh0HK2MNhHqI5TsanpgkWZcsex2iB5q2auNAQIEyQumm7p8E98_jD9jnrpwKI5rxIpYoE9SUEHoJCUC10f2SAq-tmpghvadcWKJaUXFGUQRshegbMSwGDRPUfc-uNH5U2NMoqFoTV38BfCHOck1-k95jLTqaIuDjP18-Fnu6o76uRwxCrJPfnm11yVi39RvJb-_8vaL0cj9pWvR4Gnc9muS5QS9ewqTIQI_uIJbR4ROseG_9tnNDCKSGA-1kvkGLm8F4JD5e4TyHf78459NncBdoN159SyJG7DVuxs3KnlqPVlm_FXHcRBAztHrFcv6Gqzbcbk7VA3Z1xGhHntJbJgY3NS_tAPDO8VgC0Hy_0xGzuMJqEZPDycyULEhEccNle8ATaDx73zSdORjqCq1mzyDnHX9DC0dKc_WxAJy5psI3pa4bW7VyAkwUEjYqTwq)

My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I produced the film Sound of Freedom, and founded the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** because I believe, without reservation, that every child deserves to be safe, and **none of them are for sale.** Right now, we are working urgently with organizations on the ground in Venezuela. # [The one endorsement I want most](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=208243283&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA4MjQzMjgzLCJpYXQiOjE3ODUwMDk3MjUsImV4cCI6MTc4NzYwMTcyNSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.kCwJjv6av_j7TCNHTFDlskjIkj32lwd0wNqfQ4L_ce8)
### Whitmer, Clyburn, Peters, Stabenow, the Congressional Black Caucus PAC, EMILY's List, the Teamsters, IronWorkers ... and YOU.
